races.name: Club 26 Heritage Handicap

runners_data.name: Run Boy Run
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here, Richard Spencer's five-year-old goes from pole and should find this a rare opportunity to dictate entirely unopposed; George Wood takes the ride but the horse has a concerning recent form string of 671200 and may be vulnerable once the field arrives to challenge him.|

runners_data.name: Dubai Bling
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old has strong recent form (1 and 2 in his last three visits to this trip and distance band) and David Probert will be able to slot in behind the leader naturally; good to firm suits him well per his sim-going record of 10 wins and six places from 12 runs.|

runners_data.name: Annaf
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's seven-year-old is a genuine hold-up type whose style fits cleanly into this race without redistribution concerns; Cieren Fallon will be waiting for a run but the recent form of 776003 and a blank sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 tries on this surface temper enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: King Of Light
runners_data.note: Harry Vigors (5lb claim) partners this Stuart Williams-trained four-year-old who arrives on the back of a win 12 days ago and has a useful record at five furlongs on good ground; his natural prominent style means he should get a clean trip behind the leader.|

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old has a strong course profile and Sean Levey knows the track well; a natural prominent racer who should slot in comfortably, though the form string of 263104 shows some inconsistency and he will need to quicken sharply on fast ground.|

runners_data.name: Adrestia
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's four-year-old is a natural pace horse with an excellent sim-going record of 13/14 on similar ground, but the volume of prominent types in this field means she is unlikely to secure her preferred berth and races with a style-fit discount as a result.|

runners_data.name: Toca Madera
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old loves five furlongs and has hit the frame repeatedly at this trip, but Luke Morris will find this 16-runner field leaves him with nowhere to go early; a horse who wants to race up with the pace will instead be chasing from midfield, which blunts his chance.|

runners_data.name: Behike
runners_data.note: George Scott's unexposed three-year-old is the most interesting young horse in the field, winning two of his last three starts; David Egan rides and the slight concern is the small sim-going sample (2 from 4) but lightly raced horses with that profile carry residual upside here.|

runners_data.name: Trefor
runners_data.note: Charles Hills's five-year-old carries a strong win record (5 wins from 15 on sim-going) but the form of 10-040 is patchy lately; naturally wants to race up with the pace, but in this crowded field Callum Rodriguez will have to be content further back than the horse would prefer.|

runners_data.name: Regal Envoy
runners_data.note: William Knight's seven-year-old is consistent at five furlongs and has four wins from 15 on similar ground, with Taylor Fisher taking a claim; the horse is a natural front-rank type whose tendency to be in the first two or three is frustrated by the sheer number of rivals wanting the same ground.|

runners_data.name: Havana Hurricane
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old was last seen just eight days ago and ran a fair third at five furlongs on good ground; Jack Mitchell will look to take up a prominent pitch and the horse has strong course-appropriate form (multiple placings at five furlongs on good going), making him competitive.|

runners_data.name: Glamorous Breeze
runners_data.note: Christopher Mason's eight-year-old mare is in excellent recent form (2-3-3 in her last three) and Gina Mangan partners her; though the redistribution to midfield is forced by the size of the field, her solid sim-going record (3 wins, 7 places) shows she handles conditions, and she often finds more than expected late.|

runners_data.name: Schrodinger's Cat
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's three-year-old boasts a perfect sim-going record of 13 from 13 runs on similar ground and has two wins and ten places from those; Oliver Stammers rides, and while the horse is naturally front-rank, being shuffled back could actually suit if he retains his ability to quicken off a true pace.|

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Charlie Pike's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up type (hg:b notes blinkers) and Kieren Fox will be riding to come late; the form of 005606 is modest and 34 days off the track is a mild concern, but the style is authentic and he is not compromised by the redistribution that affects so many rivals.|

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby's four-year-old has won three of his last six starts and carries headgear (t/ce), with Maxime Guyon in the saddle; despite being squeezed into midfield by the crowded nature of this field, the horse is in form and the low OR of 83 means a big weight advantage that could offset the positional disadvantage.|

runners_data.name: Mesaafi
runners_data.note: Ross Burdon's five-year-old wears blinkers and Kieran O'Neill rides; the horse's form of -08414 is limited and a sim-going record of just 1 win from 15 on similar conditions makes it hard to fancy, regardless of the pace scenario, with the redistribution from his natural position adding another layer of difficulty.|

races.paceDynamic: Run Boy Run is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner sprint, and with no genuine challenger for the lead he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates on Good to Firm ground at Ascot. Behind him, Dubai Bling, King Of Light, Fandom, Behike and Havana Hurricane will compete for the prominent positions that immediately follow, creating a defined but not chaotic early order. The field is saturated with natural front-running and prominent types — Toca Madera, Adrestia, Schrodinger's Cat, Regal Envoy, Trefor, Glamorous Breeze, Ancient State and Mesaafi are all genuine front-rank horses who will be squeezed back into midfield by sheer volume, racing out of their preferred role. With Run Boy Run setting an uncontested, honest-but-not-suicidal tempo on fast ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace in the first three to six — those racing prominently in their natural position will get first run, while the crowded midfield is likely to find traffic a bigger problem than the pace itself.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Run Boy Run Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Run Boy Run settles into an uncontested lead and sets a measured, gallop-friendly tempo that suits horses who track the pace.
scenarios.body: Run Boy Run dictates from the front at a sustainable clip on Good to Firm Ascot turf, and horses who are able to travel prominently in genuine positions — Dubai Bling, King Of Light, Fandom — get first run at the two-furlong pole and have the ground to quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Leaders Fade
scenarios.trigger: If Run Boy Run goes faster than comfortable and the race develops into a true test of stamina that benefits horses coming from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: A stronger early tempo stretches the field out and allows horses like Behike, who is lightly raced and unexposed over the trip, and Havana Hurricane to pounce from a tracking position in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Flyer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compress the field and allow one of the redistributed prominent types to sprint through a gap late.
scenarios.body: Schrodinger's Cat or Glamorous Breeze — both natural front-rank horses nudged into midfield by the crowd — finds daylight and runs on strongly, benefiting from having been settled rather than scrubbing along in traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field bunches, allowing genuine hold-up horses to sprint through on the wide outside.
scenarios.body: Annaf or Brosay, both true hold-up types whose style is not compromised by the redistribution problem, get a clear passage and land late blows as the leaders tire in the final 50 yards.

watchPoints.text: Run Boy Run sets the entire tempo of this race — if George Wood allows him to stride on unchallenged, a horse tracking him closely (Dubai Bling or King Of Light) gets first run and a clear passage; if he is reined in too tightly, the whole field compresses and traffic becomes the defining factor.

With eight or more horses naturally wanting prominent positions squeezed into a midfield that only fits three or four runners, watch for a hectic first two furlongs as Toca Madera, Adrestia, Regal Envoy and Schrodinger's Cat all try to push forward — any significant bump or check near the rail could be costly at this tight five-furlong trip.

Schrodinger's Cat's sim-going record of 13 from 13 on similar conditions is statistically exceptional and warrants respect even if the redistribution to midfield complicates his chance — Oliver Stammers will need a clean passage but the horse has the profile to outrun his mapped position if he finds daylight late.

Ancient State's low official rating of 83 gives him a substantial weight-in-hand advantage over the top weights and his recent form of 122511 is sharp; Maxime Guyon is an elite jockey in this company, and if the horse can get even close to his natural front-rank position he will be carrying far less than rivals of comparable ability.

Behike is the most unexposed three-year-old in the field with only four career runs, and a win at six furlongs followed by two wins at shorter trips suggests the five-furlong trip on fast ground could unlock him — watch how David Egan positions him in the first furlong, as his best form has come from a tracking role.

races.name: Juddmonte Summer Mile Stakes (Group 2) (Rnd)

runners_data.name: No Lunch
runners_data.note: A five-year-old in fine form with four consecutive wins, but all recent successes came abroad on Standard and Slow surfaces — the Good to Firm Ascot ground is an unknown quantity, and his natural desire to race prominently will be frustrated here with More Thunder already in that role.

runners_data.name: Docklands
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's six-year-old has strong course form on Good ground (13 similar-going runs) and was third here last time, giving him a live angle; races prominently and can slot in just off More Thunder in a genuine position, making him one of the cleaner tactical fits.

runners_data.name: Holloway Boy
runners_data.note: Burke's veteran has been consistent without winning, placing in nine of his last 15 runs, but a run of five races without a victory and a sequence of placed efforts suggests he finds one or two too good at this level; his naturally prominent style will be crowded out here, forcing him to race out of role.

runners_data.name: Jonquil
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old has course and distance form and a strong record on similar going (10 of 12 runs), but a nine-run sequence without a win including two distant last-place efforts raises questions about current consistency; pushed into midfield by the pace congestion, his effectiveness is diminished.

runners_data.name: More Thunder
runners_data.note: William Haggas's five-year-old is the key pace-setter and highest-rated runner on OR, with Fallon booked and a 12-from-56 trainer strike-rate in the 14-day window — confirmed solo front-runner who sets the entire tactical context of this race, and his form of two wins followed by two seconds is solid at this level.

runners_data.name: Naqeeb
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with zero wins from five similar-going runs and has been stepping back down from longer trips; the drop to a mile may suit but the lack of a win from 14 comparable-going efforts is a persistent concern.

runners_data.name: Seagulls Eleven
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old arrives on the back of two consecutive wins and races from off the pace; both wins came on Soft ground, giving a slight concern on Good to Firm Ascot, though a placed effort on Good shows he is not inconvenienced by quicker conditions.

runners_data.name: Zeus Olympios
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's four-year-old has an excellent record on similar going (6 of 7 runs) and two wins at the highest recent level, though four consecutive races without a win suggest his form has levelled; Sam James rides and he is the most natural prominent type alongside More Thunder with the tactical position to challenge.

races.paceDynamic: More Thunder is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press him hard from the outset, Cieren Fallon should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground around Ascot's round mile. The field is deceptively pace-heavy — No Lunch, Jonquil, and Holloway Boy are all naturally prominent types, but with More Thunder already occupying that role and the race shape compressing, those three are likely to be shuffled into midfield against their instincts, compromising their effectiveness. Zeus Olympios and Docklands are the two prominent runners best equipped to track More Thunder from a genuine position, while Naqeeb and Seagulls Eleven operate as true hold-up horses with the tactical patience to wait. A controlled front-running pace on a flat, fast surface over a mile at Ascot historically rewards those who can sustain their effort from the front or sit just off a solo leader in a rhythm — the profile that benefits most is the one to two horses who can track More Thunder without burning energy in a positional battle, and then challenge him with a genuine turn of foot in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: More Thunder Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If More Thunder is allowed to stride on uncontested and sets a steady-to-honest pace that tests stamina without inviting a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: More Thunder dictates from the front under Fallon, and the race resolves into a test of who can sustain their run closest to him — Zeus Olympios and Docklands, tracking smoothly just behind, are ideally positioned to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If More Thunder's pace is honest enough to soften him late and one of the tracking prominent runners delivers a clean late thrust.
scenarios.body: Zeus Olympios or Docklands, sitting two to three lengths off the pace in a comfortable rhythm, pounces inside the final furlong as More Thunder's effort flattens; their ability to race close to the pace without expending early energy is decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Comes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and create genuine end-to-end pace, leaving the back-markers with ground to make up but a truly run race to pick off.
scenarios.body: Seagulls Eleven or Naqeeb, held up off a hot gallop, finds the clearest run through a tiring field in the final furlong — Seagulls Eleven's two recent wins and course suitability on this going make it the more credible late threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Unsettle Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion of prominent runners causes a tactical scramble early, unsettling More Thunder's rhythm and producing a messy, falsely-run race.
scenarios.body: No Lunch, Jonquil, or Holloway Boy, unable to settle in midfield against their natural instincts, push forward and disrupt the pace, creating an uneven gallop that could benefit a versatile type capable of adapting mid-race.

watchPoints.text: More Thunder (Cieren Fallon) goes unchallenged to the front — if he is allowed a completely uncontested lead, the race effectively begins at the two-furlong pole and his stamina could see him last all the way home.

No Lunch, Jonquil, and Holloway Boy — all natural front-runners — risk over-racing or causing early interference as they are squeezed out of their preferred position by More Thunder's early lead, potentially disrupting the rhythm of those immediately behind them.

Seagulls Eleven's two recent wins came on Soft ground; if the Good to Firm going at Ascot proves quicker than ideal, his late finishing effort may not materialise to the same degree, making him vulnerable in any scenario that requires him to quicken sharply.

Docklands (George Wood, Harry Eustace) is the most experienced horse in the race at this course on this going (13 of 15 runs on similar ground) — any market confidence on the day deserves respect given his tactical familiarity with the track.
Trainer K.R. Burke saddles two runners (Zeus Olympios and Holloway Boy) — watch for any stable drift or support that might indicate which is considered the more fancied runner from the yard.

races.name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Ascot Hospitality Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Anniversary
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Ralph Beckett who stays this trip well and has placed twice over 2m and 14f on good ground recently — 41 days off is not a concern for this yard, but she needs more pace than one front-runner is likely to generate and will be produced very late.

runners_data.name: Fireblade
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's five-year-old lands the lone front-running slot and will enjoy the absence of any rival to press him — 14 days since last run is fine, though his deeper history includes a distant 17th over 18f suggesting trip limits matter, and the 0.93 style-fit flag is irrelevant here as he genuinely owns the lead.

runners_data.name: Divine Knight
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner with strong 1W2P form on good ground and Cieren Fallon booked, but his best efforts have come over shorter trips (8-10f) and he arrives as a prominent racer who is likely to find himself sitting further back than ideal in this field, which softens the chance.

runners_data.name: Artisan Dancer
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Charlie Johnston who has struggled in recent starts over 16f at Southwell and Goodwood; all five recent outings have produced modest finishes and, though he wants to race prominently, he will be shuffled back in this traffic and his form does not inspire confidence in any position.

runners_data.name: Galilean Quality
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's lightly-raced three-year-old is the freshest horse in the field on the class climb, carries the lowest weight at 128lbs, and has won twice from seven runs on good-to-soft or standard; only one run on pure good ground — that form needs to translate to Good to Firm before he is fully trusted.

runners_data.name: King Of Berkshire
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's progressive three-year-old has an excellent 2W5P record on good ground and won over 12f at Ascot last time, giving him a live course-and-distance angle; David Probert rides and he is a genuine prominent racer who must hope to secure a forward berth — if he does, his profile is among the most relevant in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Fireblade is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and will set out to dictate from the front over this 1m6f trip at Ascot on Good to Firm ground, with no natural rival to press him through the early stages. Behind him, Divine Knight, Artisan Dancer, and King Of Berkshire are all genuine prominent-type horses who cannot all occupy their natural position — the field holds more pace-hungry runners than the race shape can accommodate, and most likely it is Galilean Quality who can slot into the second or third slot given his recent course form, with the redistributed prominent horses forced to sit deeper than they prefer. Anniversary, a hold-up type, will be brought widest and latest. The race shape strongly favours a patient mid-to-hold-up profile that can travel efficiently off a single uncontested leader before producing a sustained finish: a lone pace-setter at Ascot over this flat, undemanding 1m6f with Good to Firm ground is classic territory for a horse who can stalk and pounce in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fireblade controls throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Fireblade is allowed to roll along uncontested and the pace is steady enough to sap closers without igniting a furious finish.
scenarios.body: Fireblade sets a measured, confidence-building gallop and never faces a meaningful challenge for the lead, arriving at the home turn with energy intact; horses who want to come from behind find the fractions too controlled to generate the sustained gallop they need to reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent stalker pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent horses manages to slot closer than expected and outlasts Fireblade in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A horse such as King Of Berkshire or Galilean Quality, travelling prominently just off the leader, benefits if Fireblade sets even a fraction too strong a pace and fades inside the final furlong; their good-ground profiles and sharp Ascot-distance form make them the most dangerous in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse finishes over
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out early, creating enough of a test to open the door for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Anniversary, dropping back from hold-up ground with recent form at the right trip and going, can pick up tired rivals if the tempo has genuinely cut into them; this scenario requires more pace than one horse alone is likely to generate, making it the least common of the plausible shapes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent pack battles home
scenarios.trigger: If two or more of the redistributed prominent horses force their way closer to Fireblade and the race becomes a contested tempo test throughout.
scenarios.body: Divine Knight or Artisan Dancer muscling forward turns the race into a group scrap for supremacy, with Fireblade potentially losing first run and stamina-resolute runners benefiting from a stop-start gallop; this shape is heavily discounted because multiple horses are tagged out of role and would need to race against their likely positioning.

watchPoints.text: Fireblade — if he jumps cleanly and is allowed to roll along without a challenge from the first bend, he could be very difficult to reel in on Good to Firm ground over this flat Ascot 1m6f trip.

King Of Berkshire — his Ascot win last time over 12f on good ground is directly relevant, but watch whether Cieren Fallon on Divine Knight crowds him early and denies him the forward position his form requires.

Galilean Quality — only one previous run on similar going and stepping up sharply from 12f; watch how he handles the extra ground in the closing stages because his wins have all been at shorter trips.

Anniversary — monitor in-running to see whether the pace is truly strong enough to bring her hold-up style into play; if Fireblade dawdles, she has no chance of closing on the leaders from her expected position at the back.

Artisan Dancer — his recent form over 16f at Southwell and Goodwood has been very poor; watch whether he is ridden with more restraint than usual given he cannot get a prominent pitch, as any early scrimmaging for position could drain him before the straight.

races.name: Side Glance Story Book Launch Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Nightime Dancer
runners_data.note: Expected to lead and likely to get an uncontested rail throughout; trainer Hannon sends a 4yo here 22 days fresh with a tongue tie, and the horse's two placed efforts at 12-14f on Good ground suggest it stays adequately, though its 0-for-8 record and modest recent form (8,2,4,4,0) raise questions about whether it can convert from the front once challenged.|

runners_data.name: Nesthorn
runners_data.note: One win from nine career starts came off a patient hold-up ride at 10f on Good, and the horse has posted five consecutive sevenths at 9-12f since — Benoit de la Sayette takes over for Baker's yard, which has landed just zero from seven in the last fortnight, so confidence is limited; will need a genuinely strong pace to find any late gap.|

runners_data.name: Green Cape
runners_data.note: Dropped to a career-low OR of 96, Simon & Ed Crisford send this 4yo back to 14f for the first time since a well-beaten 16th; tongue tie fitted and only three places from ten runs on Good ground is a poor record in these conditions, but a prominent style suits this likely race shape well.|

runners_data.name: Ernst Blofeld
runners_data.note: Landed a win at 12f on Standard going for Al Jehani's yard but has run poorly on Good ground (7th, 4th, 14th, 15th in four tries) — the going switch is a clear question mark, and Callum Rodriguez picks up the ride for a trainer with zero wins from 12 in the last 14 days; holds a genuine hold-up style that this controlled-pace scenario may not reward.|

runners_data.name: Tycoon
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's 4yo carries a prominent-racing profile that suits this race shape directly; David Egan takes the ride and the horse's placed effort at 9f on Good (3rd) plus a win at 8f shows it can travel prominently, though stepping up to 1m4f for the first time is a distance question worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Ghaiyya
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard has been prolific (9/67 in 14 days) and Jack Mitchell rides a horse who has won four of 15 runs at 11-13f on Good ground — the concern is that its natural prominent-racing tendency puts it in competition for a position that is already occupied, and with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93, finishing from further back than it likes is a real tactical disadvantage here.|

runners_data.name: Tryfan
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's 5yo returns after 58 days off the track — the longest absence in the field — and its hold-up profile is genuine, with three placed efforts at 12-14f on Tapeta/Standard; the switch to Good to Firm Ascot turf is an untested surface combination for this horse, and being pushed out of its natural rear position makes it harder to assess.|

runners_data.name: Blue Hercules
runners_data.note: A 3yo carrying the lowest weight at 114lbs for Muir & Grassick, who have gone winless in 18 runs over 14 days; its hold-up profile is authentic but the horse's only placed effort (2nd, 10f Good) came when racing more handily than expected — four runs on Good ground without a win, and operating outside its natural race position here, limits the case for it.|

races.paceDynamic: Nightime Dancer is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 1m4f Good to Firm Ascot handicap and is almost certain to lead from the gates, with no genuine challenger for that position — the pace will be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured, suiting a horse that can dictate its own rhythm. Green Cape and Tycoon are the natural prominent types who will look to sit just off the leader, though neither has the profile to push Nightime Dancer into a contested gallop. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all occupy their natural positions — Ghaiyya, Blue Hercules, and Tryfan are genuine pace-seeking or hold-up horses redistributed into midfield because the map is already full at the front and rear; of those, Ghaiyya is most likely to push forward and actually claim a prominent berth if rivals slot in, while Blue Hercules and Tryfan are the ones most compromised by this congestion. A lone leader in control over 1m4f on Good to Firm Ascot ground with no pace pressure heavily favours horses who can race prominently and travel into the race with cover — patient midfield closers with genuine hold-up profiles will need a strong late pace injection that this shape is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Nightime Dancer leads unchallenged and sets a measured, uncontested gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Nightime Dancer dictates every fraction from the front, the field strings out at a fair but unspectacular pace, and the race resolves into a stamina test from the home turn where prominent trackers hold the edge over late closers. Tycoon and Green Cape, sitting within striking range of the leader in second or third, are ideally placed to pounce without having to find extra ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If Ghaiyya successfully forces its way to a prominent pitch and travels strongly into the straight.
scenarios.body: The pace remains steady but Ghaiyya, able to reclaim its natural front-rank position, sits closer than its mapped slot suggests and delivers a strong run from two out before the true hold-up horses can close. This shape amplifies the chance of horses who can race handily without burning fuel, and Ghaiyya's recent 1-2 form at 12-13f on similar ground is directly relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough for true closers to reel in the prominent brigade.
scenarios.body: Nesthorn and Ernst Blofeld, racing from their natural hold-up positions at the rear of the small field, would require the front-runners to go hard enough to tie each other up — unlikely with only one confirmed leader — but not impossible if Ghaiyya pushes the pace from behind. Nesthorn's one win came from well off the pace at 10f, and Ernst Blofeld has a win at 12f on Standard; both need a truly run race that this shape is unlikely to generate at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If a slow start, interference, or unexpected pace injection from the rear disrupts the expected processional shape.
scenarios.body: A low-probability scenario where Blue Hercules or Tryfan, both redistributed hold-up types operating out of role, find the race collapsing into a sprint finish from two out that briefly suits a wide-margin closer. The shape would need to fall apart completely for this to materialise given the small field and the likely steady tempo set by one unopposed leader.

watchPoints.text: Ghaiyya (Mitchell/Johnston) is likely to push forward from its mapped midfield position into a natural prominent slot — if it secures cover just off the leader, its four wins at this trip on Good ground make it a serious threat to the race-shape beneficiaries.|

Nightime Dancer's record of zero wins from eight starts and a recent form string of 8,2,4,4,0 raises the question of whether it can hold its advantage once pressed from the home turn — any fade opens the race for horses immediately on its back.|

Tycoon is unproven beyond 10f and faces a career-first run over 1m4f — if the step up in trip finds it out in the final two furlongs, the race shape that should suit it most becomes a liability rather than an asset.|

Nesthorn's recent sequence of five consecutive 7th-place finishes on Good ground is a significant pattern flag — even in a scenario that superficially suits hold-up horses, the horse's inability to convert from that position is worth noting before assuming it improves.|

The going for this race is officially Good to Firm (confirmed in the going report for the 4:12 slot), despite the race header listing Good — horses flagged going=OK were assessed on Good, so the firmer surface is worth monitoring for any last-minute market moves suggesting concern.|

races.name: Racing To Zero Fillies' Handicap (Str)

runners_data.name: Nanino Niyati
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows hold-up filly whose form figures of 1-1 on Good ground are compelling, but she needs something to aim at on this straight mile and a controlled pace from Blingy's Sister is unlikely to play to her strengths; 40 days since last run needs noting.

runners_data.name: Sprightly Dance
runners_data.note: Roger Varian hold-up type whose single good-ground win came over a mile, but her recent form on Soft-to-Standard is more encouraging than Good, and she looks set to be further back than ideal with so many prominent types in the field.

runners_data.name: Revelance
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly is a genuine prominent racer with a win at 8f on Soft and a solid placed run on Good, making the step onto Good to Firm a minor question; a 12-day turnaround for a busy trainer who fires 7/51 in the 14-day window adds quiet interest.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Jane Chapple-Hyam who has a win on Good ground over 8f but a worrying 28th-of-28 on similar terms last time, and her last five runs at a higher level suggest she needs to find significant improvement to be a factor.

runners_data.name: Blingy's Sister
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter who will lead from the front for Hugo Palmer and David Probert; she has Good-ground form to point to but is technically running as a prominent type at slightly shorter odds than her role warrants, and her style fit score suggests she could be vulnerable if the pace she sets flatters rivals.

runners_data.name: Rosa Inglesa
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes three-year-old with three placed efforts on Good ground over 7-8f and a form figure of 1 over this trip on Soft, making the slightly faster conditions a query; Kaiya Fraser takes over in the saddle and she is set up perfectly to track the pace from second or third.

runners_data.name: Thaluna
runners_data.note: William Haggas prominent filly whose 3-2 in her last two over 8f on Good demonstrates this trip and ground suit her well; Cieren Fallon's booking for one of the sport's premier yards is always worth noting, and 41 days since last run is not unusual for Haggas.

runners_data.name: Star Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley runner returning from 272 days off the track, and while her natural racing style is prominent, she is pushed into a midfield map position by the number of pace-seeking types in this field; the lengthy layoff on top of being out of role makes her a very difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Celestra
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden three-year-old whose most recent win came over this exact trip on Good ground, and she wears a hood (headgear noted); naturally a front-rank racer, she will find herself operating further back than she'd like because of the competition for prominent positions, which tempers confidence despite strong raw form.

runners_data.name: Hot And Cold
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly has back-to-back wins and arrives just 11 days after her last run, typical of Prescott's production-line approach; she is a true prominent type whose run style has been redistributed to midfield here — her winning chance hinges on getting a pitch closer to the pace than the map suggests she will find available.

races.paceDynamic: Blingy's Sister is the confirmed pace-setter and will dictate from the front on this straight mile at Ascot on Good to Firm ground, setting a sustainable and uncontested tempo that should keep the race honest without ever becoming a sprint from the gates. Rosa Inglesa, Revelance, and Thaluna are genuine prominent types who will look to track close to the lead, creating a compact early order that keeps pressure on without generating a true false pace. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions — Celestra, Hot And Cold, and Star Of Dubai are true prominent racers who will be squeezed into a midfield role they don't naturally occupy, making their tasks harder and their winning chances more dependent on an untypical performance. With a single controlled pace-setter and a bunched prominent group just off it, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently in the first four and quicken from there, rather than genuine hold-up types who will need something to go wrong up front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Blingy's Sister sets a controlled, sustainable pace and the prominent stalkers — Rosa Inglesa, Revelance, Thaluna — travel smoothly just off it before producing their winning effort in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A steady gallop on Good to Firm Ascot puts a premium on horses who can take a prominent pitch and produce a clean turn of foot from close to the pace, avoiding the traffic that will afflict those shuffled back into midfield; the straight mile rewards those who travel into the race rather than chase it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Blingy's Sister dictates at a genuinely pedestrian pace that produces a sprint-finish and rewards whoever can quicken from the front.
scenarios.body: A slow, strung-out race where the leader builds an unassailable rhythm and rivals in behind never get competitive until too late; prominent types closest to the action benefit most if the pace proves generous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and the race becomes a tactical crawl that opens a gap for genuine hold-up horses to swoop late.
scenarios.body: Nanino Niyati and Sprightly Dance would need the leaders to tie each other up and a strong finishing run to be delivered in the straight; this is the least structurally likely shape given the redistribution of prominent types who are not true closers anyway.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Pressure Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse to settle into midfield roles and push forward to contest the pace with Blingy's Sister, creating a genuinely hot gallop.
scenarios.body: An elevated tempo on fast ground would compromise the front runners but could bring hold-up horses and the freshest legs into play late on the straight; Nanino Niyati is the likeliest beneficiary if the pace proves genuinely strong.

watchPoints.text: Celestra and Hot And Cold are both natural front-rank racers mapped to midfield — watch in the early stages whether either pushes forward to contest the pace, because if two or more do, the tempo will increase sharply and reshape the entire race.

Star Of Dubai returns from 272 days off the track and will need to slot into a midfield role against her natural instincts; if she dwells or misses the break, she could cause interference to hold-up horses Nanino Niyati and Sprightly Dance.

Harlequin Breeze posted a 28th-of-28 on similar Good ground last time and faces a sharp fitness or confidence question; monitor her in the market and in the pre-race parade for signs she is not at her best.

Blingy's Sister's uncontested lead will be the race's defining structural feature — if she is pressed by any of the redistributed prominent types from the outset, the scenario probabilities shift substantially toward hold-up horses.

Thaluna's jockey booking (Cieren Fallon for Haggas) and recent form over this exact trip and going make her the most likely prominent horse to capitalise if the pace is moderate — watch her market move in the final hour before racing.

races.name: Thames Hospice Trunks Across The Thames Handicap

runners_data.name: Winston's Warrior
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here with a clear path to the lead; Charles Hills yard has form and Harry Vigors claims 5lb, though trainer's 14-day strike rate of 1/17 tempers confidence; similar-going form shows only one placed run from five and it is racing out of natural role as a hold-up type, so a front-running switch is a significant style change.

runners_data.name: Port Road
runners_data.note: Simon Dow yard at 0/5 in the past fortnight; true hold-up performer with two wins at 7f on standard ground but a poor record on good; awkward wide draw in a big field makes cover hard to find.

runners_data.name: Havana Blue
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's in-form stable (4/20 last 14 days) gives this consistent mare a yard angle; best similar-going record of the confirmed hold-up runners (11/15 starts) and has placed three times on comparable ground; likely needs room in the straight to be effective.

runners_data.name: Cancan In The Rain
runners_data.note: Ran two wins and a second from her last four starts and brings strong staying power over this trip on good ground; races prominently by style so the controlled pace suits perfectly; visor fitted, which has previously sharpened her responses.

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: A genuine back-of-the-field operator by nature but the oversupply of hold-up horses means it will be filed into midfield against its instincts; trainer at 0/1 in the 14-day window; recent form over 6f suggests this longer trip should suit better, though good ground record is mixed.

runners_data.name: Enola Grey
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty sends this mare in reasonable form with a recent win at 7f on standard ground; naturally sits off the pace but current race shape forces closer positioning; no wins from four starts on comparable good ground adds caution.

runners_data.name: Documenting
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old veteran who finds himself bumped out of his natural deep-closing role due to the field's composition; Kevin & Lauren Frost yard at 0/16 over 14 days; did manage a placed effort over 7f on good recently but the age and repositioning are both concerns.

runners_data.name: Arantes Nascimento
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's horse has placed four times from five similar-going starts without winning, suggesting solid but frustrating form; races prominently and will be competitive early; four placed runs at 7f on standard and good ground make this a genuine market mover in this scenario.

runners_data.name: North View
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams at 0/18 in a fortnight, and this horse's recent string of finishing positions (8,7,13,4,7) reads as inconsistent; its true hold-up style is squeezed into midfield by the crowded rear; headgear change to a hood may sharpen focus but the yard form undermines confidence.

runners_data.name: Red Hat Eagle
runners_data.note: William Knight (2/21 in 14 days) sends this horse in on its recent run of placed efforts; naturally wants to come from behind but has been pushed forward on the map; headgear (p) fitted, and has placed twice from 15 good-ground starts showing some capability on this surface.

runners_data.name: Be Frank
runners_data.note: Ian Williams (3/36 in 14 days) and David Egan combine; this one's best form has come on soft ground and it has struggled to win on good; hooded and naturally a hold-up type, it has been mapped to midfield ahead of its preferred station.

runners_data.name: Beauty By My Side
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's 4-year-old returns after 143 days off — the longest layoff in the field — and that absence is the dominant concern; naturally held up and shuffled forward; did win at 8f on standard ground last time but stamping authority off a big break is a tall ask.

runners_data.name: Luansobe
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes's 3-year-old has won at 7f on standard ground and brings a tidy form line of 20-10 for its age; only four career runs on similar going (2/4) so sample is thin; races held-up and at 3 in a veteran-heavy field will need to settle quickly.

runners_data.name: Lunario
runners_data.note: Luke Dace's 6-year-old has an eye-catching two wins and three places from 15 good-ground outings, though the form string of 8-9700 recently is discouraging; shifted forward from its preferred rear position and fitted with tongue-tie and visor; current form cycle doesn't support confidence.

runners_data.name: Sponsor
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's 3-year-old is tagged as fading in the finish — a critical flag in a 7f race — and its recent form of 94300 with all five similar-going runs non-winning speaks clearly; tongue-tie fitted but the fade flag means it is hard to support regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Ararat
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook & John Bridger's mare showed a third at 7f good and a fourth recently; one of the horses pushed into midfield from its natural back-of-the-field position; no wins from 15 good-ground tries but has placed once, and the low OR of 68 gives a fine weight advantage if everything clicks.

runners_data.name: Oceti
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon (9/46 in 14 days) and Sean Levey is a notable combination at this course; however, Oceti's recent form reads 6-806 and it has failed to place in any of its four similar-going starts; in the redistribution cluster and currently out of form.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Ross Burdon's 6-year-old won over 7f on good ground recently and has placed four times from 15 similar-going starts including three wins; lowest OR in the field (66) gives maximum weight relief; naturally a hold-up horse placed into midfield, but if it can sneak wide and produce its finishing effort, the form profile is competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Winston's Warrior is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead in an 18-runner handicap, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 7f Ascot straight. Cancan In The Rain and Arantes Nascimento will press from prominent positions, creating a modest but organised early tempo rather than a contested burn-out. The field is stuffed with hold-up horses — Daring Legend, Documenting, Oceti, North View, Red Hat Eagle, Be Frank, Beauty By My Side, Lunario, Ararat, and Northcliff all want to race further back than the map can accommodate, meaning several will be shuffled into unfamiliar midfield berths and unable to get their natural position. On good-to-firm ground at Ascot where a controlled pace with a clear early leader is the norm, the race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — genuine closers will have too much to do from out of position and may find the race over before the straight opens up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Winston's Warrior dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent horses track within striking distance.
scenarios.body: Winston's Warrior sets a comfortable clip with Cancan In The Rain and Arantes Nascimento close up, and the race becomes a test of sustained stamina on fast ground rather than a finishing sprint; the winner will be among those who race on the pace and hit the rising ground running.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Cancan In The Rain or Arantes Nascimento travel smoothly off the pace-setter and kick clear inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The controlled early gallop allows both prominent types to conserve energy and deliver a sustained run under fair weights; Cancan In The Rain's recent wins and course-compatible form make it a prime beneficiary if it can slot into second gear early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Held-Up Runner Gaps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a true closer threads through late.
scenarios.body: Havana Blue or Enola Grey, both genuine hold-up types with decent going form, would need a strung-out field and a clear run to pick off tiring rivals; Havana Blue has the most relevant similar-going form of this group but faces the challenge of getting daylight in an 18-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Rough Race
scenarios.trigger: If the overloaded midfield causes traffic issues and the race falls apart tactically, opening the door to an unconventional winner.
scenarios.body: The sheer number of hold-up horses forced into unnatural midfield spots risks bunching, interference, and a fractured finish; a lightly weighted runner like Northcliff, who has recent winning form over similar ground and trip, could exploit gaps if positioned on the outside.

watchPoints.text: Winston's Warrior leads uncontested but is a hold-up type switched to the front — watch whether it is comfortable in front or idles and gets caught by the prominent pair in the final furlong.

With ten horses redistributed from their preferred rear positions into an already-crowded midfield, watch for significant traffic interference and potential interference claims in the straight particularly involving Be Frank, North View, and Lunario.

Cancan In The Rain's visor and recent winning form make it a pace shape beneficiary, but it is trained by Gihan Arnolda whose 14-day strike rate is 0/4 — watch whether the horse travels as smoothly as its form suggests it should.
Beauty By My Side returns after 143 days absent — the longest break in the field — watch its early-race behaviour and whether it settles, as a fresh horse may over-race and empty late.

Northcliff has the lowest official rating and was a recent 7f winner on good ground; watch its drawn position and whether Callum Rodriguez can manoeuvre to a clear outside run, as the weight-for-age advantage combined with the form is worth monitoring.
